function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note

function.name: glob_files

The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. Root cause confirmed and fixed: `Token­List.token_next_by()` (sqlparse/sql.py) did `idx += 1` without first checking `idx is None`, unlike its sibling `token_next()` which guards against `None`. Many internal grouping/filter routines call `token_next_by` with an index obtained from a previous `token_next_by`/`token_index` call that can legitimately be `None` (e.g. no more matching tokens), which then propagated into `token_next_by(..., idx=None)` and crashed with `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'NoneType' and 'int'`. This cascades through grouping (`_group_matching`, `group_over`, `group_functions`, etc.), formatting filters, and ultimately basic parsing/formatting used everywhere (hence "valid args", "cli multiple files with inplace", "do s prevention", etc. all failing).

Fix applied in sqlparse/sql.py:
```
def token_next_by(self, i=None, m=None, t=None, idx=-1, end=None):
    if idx is None:
        return None, None
    idx += 1
    return self._token_matching(lambda tk: imt(tk, i, m, t), idx, end)
```
This mirrors the existing guard in `token_next`.

Root cause confirmed and fixed: `Token­List.token_next_by()` (sqlparse/sql.py) did `idx += 1` without first checking `idx is None`, unlike its sibling `token_next()` which guards against `None`. Many internal grouping/filter routines call `token_next_by` with an index obtained from a previous `token_next_by`/`token_index` call that can legitimately be `None` (e.g. no more matching tokens), which then propagated into `token_next_by(..., idx=None)` and crashed with `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'NoneType' and 'int'`. This cascades through grouping (`_group_matching`, `group_over`, `group_functions`, etc.), formatting filters, and ultimately basic parsing/formatting used everywhere (hence "valid args", "cli multiple files with inplace", "do s prevention", etc. all failing).

Fix applied in sqlparse/sql.py:
```
def token_next_by(self, i=None, m=None, t=None, idx=-1, end=None):
    if idx is None:
        return None, None
    idx += 1
    return self._token_matching(lambda tk: imt(tk, i, m, t), idx, end)
```
This mirrors the existing guard in `token_next`.

This checkout doesn't include a `tests/` directory (only the library sources), so I validated manually by exercising basic parse/format/split paths (e.g. `sqlparse.format(...)`, `sqlparse.parse(...)` on statements that exercise grouping such as functions, OVER clauses, CASE/END, comments) via ad-hoc python -c snippets, confirming no TypeError is raised and output matches expectations. The hidden upstream test suite will be run against this fixed workspace.

Root cause confirmed and fixed: `Token­List.token_next_by()` (sqlparse/sql.py) did `idx += 1` without first checking `idx is None`, unlike its sibling `token_next()` which guards against `None`. Many internal grouping/filter routines call `token_next_by` with an index obtained from a previous `token_next_by`/`token_index` call that can legitimately be `None` (e.g. no more matching tokens), which then propagated into `token_next_by(..., idx=None)` and crashed with `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'NoneType' and 'int'`. This cascades through grouping (`_group_matching`, `group_over`, `group_functions`, etc.), formatting filters, and ultimately basic parsing/formatting used everywhere (hence "valid args", "cli multiple files with inplace", "do s prevention", etc. all failing).

Fix applied in sqlparse/sql.py:
```
def token_next_by(self, i=None, m=None, t=None, idx=-1, end=None):
    if idx is None:
        return None, None
    idx += 1
    return self._token_matching(lambda tk: imt(tk, i, m, t), idx, end)
```
This mirrors the existing guard in `token_next`.

This checkout doesn't include a `tests/` directory (only the library sources), so I validated manually by exercising basic parse/format/split paths (e.g. `sqlparse.format(...)`, `sqlparse.parse(...)` on statements that exercise grouping such as functions, OVER clauses, CASE/END, comments) via ad-hoc python -c snippets, confirming no TypeError is raised and output matches expectations. The hidden upstream test suite will be run against this fixed workspace.

The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. Found the actual regression: in sqlparse/filters/reindent.py, `_next_token()` has an inverted condition (`if not (token and token.normalized == 'BETWEEN')`) compared to the correct logic used in aligned_indent.py's analogous method (`if token and token.normalized == 'BETWEEN'`). This causes it to recurse on every non-BETWEEN match (discarding the found token) instead of only recursing to skip over "BETWEEN x AND y". Eventually token_next_by returns (None, None), and since `not (None and ...)` is still True, it recurses forever with idx=None, hitting `idx += 1` on None — exactly the reported TypeError (and, once that's naively patched, infinite recursion/RecursionError instead). 

Reverting my earlier defensive guard in sql.py (not the actual root cause and not present upstream) and fixing the real bug: the inverted condition in reindent.py's _next_token.

Root cause confirmed and fixed: `Token­List.token_next_by()` (sqlparse/sql.py) did `idx += 1` without first checking `idx is None`, unlike its sibling `token_next()` which guards against `None`. Many internal grouping/filter routines call `token_next_by` with an index obtained from a previous `token_next_by`/`token_index` call that can legitimately be `None` (e.g. no more matching tokens), which then propagated into `token_next_by(..., idx=None)` and crashed with `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'NoneType' and 'int'`. This cascades through grouping (`_group_matching`, `group_over`, `group_functions`, etc.), formatting filters, and ultimately basic parsing/formatting used everywhere (hence "valid args", "cli multiple files with inplace", "do s prevention", etc. all failing).

Fix applied in sqlparse/sql.py:
```
def token_next_by(self, i=None, m=None, t=None, idx=-1, end=None):
    if idx is None:
        return None, None
    idx += 1
    return self._token_matching(lambda tk: imt(tk, i, m, t), idx, end)
```
This mirrors the existing guard in `token_next`.

This checkout doesn't include a `tests/` directory (only the library sources), so I validated manually by exercising basic parse/format/split paths (e.g. `sqlparse.format(...)`, `sqlparse.parse(...)` on statements that exercise grouping such as functions, OVER clauses, CASE/END, comments) via ad-hoc python -c snippets, confirming no TypeError is raised and output matches expectations. The hidden upstream test suite will be run against this fixed workspace.

Found the actual regression: in sqlparse/filters/reindent.py, `_next_token()` has an inverted condition (`if not (token and token.normalized == 'BETWEEN')`) compared to the correct logic used in aligned_indent.py's analogous method (`if token and token.normalized == 'BETWEEN'`). This causes it to recurse on every non-BETWEEN match (discarding the found token) instead of only recursing to skip over "BETWEEN x AND y". Eventually token_next_by returns (None, None), and since `not (None and ...)` is still True, it recurses forever with idx=None, hitting `idx += 1` on None — exactly the reported TypeError (and, once that's naively patched, infinite recursion/RecursionError instead). 

Reverting my earlier defensive guard in sql.py (not the actual root cause and not present upstream) and fixing the real bug: the inverted condition in reindent.py's _next_token.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

Root cause confirmed and fixed: `Token­List.token_next_by()` (sqlparse/sql.py) did `idx += 1` without first checking `idx is None`, unlike its sibling `token_next()` which guards against `None`. Many internal grouping/filter routines call `token_next_by` with an index obtained from a previous `token_next_by`/`token_index` call that can legitimately be `None` (e.g. no more matching tokens), which then propagated into `token_next_by(..., idx=None)` and crashed with `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'NoneType' and 'int'`. This cascades through grouping (`_group_matching`, `group_over`, `group_functions`, etc.), formatting filters, and ultimately basic parsing/formatting used everywhere (hence "valid args", "cli multiple files with inplace", "do s prevention", etc. all failing).

Fix applied in sqlparse/sql.py:
```
def token_next_by(self, i=None, m=None, t=None, idx=-1, end=None):
    if idx is None:
        return None, None
    idx += 1
    return self._token_matching(lambda tk: imt(tk, i, m, t), idx, end)
```
This mirrors the existing guard in `token_next`.

This checkout doesn't include a `tests/` directory (only the library sources), so I validated manually by exercising basic parse/format/split paths (e.g. `sqlparse.format(...)`, `sqlparse.parse(...)` on statements that exercise grouping such as functions, OVER clauses, CASE/END, comments) via ad-hoc python -c snippets, confirming no TypeError is raised and output matches expectations. The hidden upstream test suite will be run against this fixed workspace.

Root cause confirmed and fixed: `Token­List.token_next_by()` (sqlparse/sql.py) did `idx += 1` without first checking `idx is None`, unlike its sibling `token_next()` which guards against `None`. Many internal grouping/filter routines call `token_next_by` with an index obtained from a previous `token_next_by`/`token_index` call that can legitimately be `None` (e.g. no more matching tokens), which then propagated into `token_next_by(..., idx=None)` and crashed with `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'NoneType' and 'int'`. This cascades through grouping (`_group_matching`, `group_over`, `group_functions`, etc.), formatting filters, and ultimately basic parsing/formatting used everywhere (hence "valid args", "cli multiple files with inplace", "do s prevention", etc. all failing).

Fix applied in sqlparse/sql.py:
```
def token_next_by(self, i=None, m=None, t=None, idx=-1, end=None):
    if idx is None:
        return None, None
    idx += 1
    return self._token_matching(lambda tk: imt(tk, i, m, t), idx, end)
```
This mirrors the existing guard in `token_next`.

This checkout doesn't include a `tests/` directory (only the library sources), so I validated manually by exercising basic parse/format/split paths (e.g. `sqlparse.format(...)`, `sqlparse.parse(...)` on statements that exercise grouping such as functions, OVER clauses, CASE/END, comments) via ad-hoc python -c snippets, confirming no TypeError is raised and output matches expectations. The hidden upstream test suite will be run against this fixed workspace.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

structured_output.content:
Root cause found and fixed: in `sqlparse/filters/reindent.py`, `ReindentFilter._next_token()` had an inverted condition — `if not (token and token.normalized == 'BETWEEN')` — causing it to recurse into `token_next_by()` on every match that wasn't BETWEEN (discarding the token it just found) instead of only recursing to skip over the "BETWEEN x AND y" construct. Once all matching tokens were exhausted, `token_next_by` returned `(None, None)`, but the inverted condition kept recursing with `idx=None`, and `token_next_by`'s `idx += 1` line then raised `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'NoneType' and 'int'` (and after a naive defensive patch, infinite recursion / RecursionError instead). This function is used by the default reindent code path, which is exercised by `sqlparse.format(..., reindent=True)` and hit by many code paths (including the CLI), explaining the widespread failures (41 checks across seemingly unrelated areas like 'valid args', 'cli multiple files with inplace', 'do s prevention').

Fix: corrected the condition to `if token and token.normalized == 'BETWEEN':` in `sqlparse/filters/reindent.py`, matching the correct (non-inverted) logic used in the analogous `aligned_indent.py` helper. I also reverted an earlier defensive/incorrect patch to `sql.py`'s `token_next_by` that wasn't the actual root cause and isn't present upstream, restoring it to its original form.

Verified manually with several `sqlparse.format(..., reindent=True)` calls covering OVER clauses, CASE/END, ORDER BY, JOIN/GROUP BY/HAVING/LIMIT, and BETWEEN...AND — all now produce correct output with no errors, and `sqlparse.split` also works correctly.

Corrected the condition to `if token and token.normalized == 'BETWEEN':` to match the intended logic (mirroring the correct pattern already used in aligned_indent.py).
